draft.details:
On early July 2026, I fell on my outstretched hand and attended the A&E department at the Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh. I was X-rayed and told it was a sprain, and I was sent home. The pain did not go away. On mid August 2026, my GP sent me back for a second X-ray, which showed a scaphoid fracture. By November 2026, the fracture has not healed and I now need surgery. I have also missed my second-year exams and had to stop shifts at my part-time job because I cannot use my wrist. I would like an explanation of what went wrong, treatment or support to put things right and compensation for what happened.

For reference, spso.org.uk (201202307.pdf) published: "We concluded, however, that the board had not provided sufficient evidence that they had carried out a thorough investigation into both x-ray incidents."
For reference, spso.org.uk (201202307.pdf) published: "We upheld Mrs C's complaints about interpretation of the x-rays, but not about their follow-up action."
I would be grateful if NHS Lothian would take these into account when looking at my complaint.
draft.location: Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh, Accident & Emergency department
draft.outcome: An explanation of what went wrong, treatment or support to put things right and compensation for what happened.
